title: Specify and validate Network-derived fracture-set sampling inputs
description: Implement the source-data boundary for the Network-based PorePy generator. Work primarily in fractopo/interop/porepy.py; add focused tests in tests/interop/test_porepy.py. Do not make PorePy a dependency. Network is the sole first-version source. Read Network.trace_data: azimuth_set_array, azimuth_array, length_array and Network.azimuth_set_names. Read observed orientation from network.trace_gdf columns named exactly dip and dip_direction (column overrides are not in scope). A usable observation has a named (non-NULL_SET) azimuth set, finite trace azimuth, finite strictly positive length, finite dip in [0, 90], and finite dip_direction in [0, 360]. Exclude every unusable observation and entire named sets with zero usable observations. Set proportions are counts of usable observations, normalized across remaining sets; do not use length weighting. Raise ValueError naming the cause if no usable observations/set remains. Keep each retained sample row intact so later sampling jointly resamples its trace azimuth, dip and dip direction, although the initial generator only uses azimuth and dip. Keep helpers pure and package-private unless a public API is needed by the generator. Use current project conventions (beartype, NumPy, clear docstrings); do not modify unfinished unrelated helpers in fractopo/interop/__init__.py.
acceptance_criteria: Tests construct a minimal Network with named sets and dip/dip_direction trace columns. Tests prove: (1) valid rows are grouped by named set; (2) NULL_SET/out-of-range/non-finite/missing orientation or non-positive-length rows are excluded; (3) proportions use usable-row counts and sum to 1; (4) an all-invalid input raises a useful ValueError; (5) automatic and manual Network set labels work because extraction consumes Network.trace_data labels. Run nix develop -c pytest tests/interop/test_porepy.py -q. Run nix develop -c prek run --all-files. Before closing: br close with test evidence, br sync --flush-only, git add -f .beads/issues.jsonl plus source/test files, and commit --no-gpg-sign with this bead id.

title: Generate PorePy 3D circular-fracture populations from Network data
description: Epic tracking the first Network-based random PorePy 3D circular-fracture exporter. Scope is deliberately empirical rather than a general statistical modelling framework: Network supplies manual/automatic set labels, trace azimuths and lengths; trace_gdf supplies dip and dip_direction. Decisions: use usable-observation count proportions; exclude invalid/unassigned observations and renormalize; sample valid rows empirically with replacement; generated strike comes from trace azimuth; dip direction is implied by right-hand rule; caller injects optional numpy.random.Generator; domain is emitted by default; centres only must be in cuboid; PorePy semi-axis is trace length / 2; all current 3D exporters are corrected likewise. Keep PorePy optional/non-dependency. Parametric/von-Mises orientation sampling, fitted-length sampling, full-disk containment, column overrides, CLI/UI work, and intersection conditioning are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Close only after children 861, zud, w0b, and hkc are closed; the focused test file, full test suite, pre-commit/lint, and documentation build (where docs changed) have passed; and the work is committed. Verify br dep cycles --json remains empty, br sync --flush-only has run, .beads/issues.jsonl is forcibly staged because .beads is ignored, and git status is clean.

title: Export seeded random circular fractures from a Network into PorePy 3D CSV
description: After 861 and zud close, implement one public exporter in fractopo/interop/porepy.py, with its unit tests in tests/interop/test_porepy.py. Suggested name: export_network_to_porepy_3d_csv_format; choose an equally explicit established-style name only if necessary. Inputs: a fractopo.analysis.network.Network, positive integer fracture_count, cuboid bounds in exact order (xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax), and optional numpy.random.Generator. No integer seed overload and no global np.random state. Reuse 861 extraction. Given ordered usable Network.azimuth_set_names, compute quotas with largest-remainder allocation: raw = proportion * fracture_count; take floors; allocate remaining count(s) to greatest fractional remainder; resolve equal remainders by original azimuth_set_names order. This guarantees exact total and deterministic quotas. For each quota, empirical-resample usable rows with replacement using rng.choice; sample centre components uniformly in inclusive mathematical bounds via rng.uniform(low, high). Use sampled trace azimuth as geological strike (convert degrees to radians); sample dip from same row (degrees to radians); do not use sampled dip_direction in output because right-hand-rule dip direction is implied by strike. Create circular EllipticalFracture values: axis=sampled trace length / 2, major_axis_angle=0. Output cuboid domain row first, followed by one eight-field row per generated fracture, validate through check_porepy_3d_csv_format, and return str. Guarantee centres only, not disk containment. Validate finite strictly increasing bounds and count > 0 before sampling. No PorePy import/dependency and no parametric distribution sampling in this first slice.
acceptance_criteria: With a seeded numpy.random.default_rng passed twice, identical input yields byte-identical CSV. Tests prove domain is the first six-field line; each later row is valid 8-field PorePy ellipse data; exact output row count equals fracture_count; quota allocation uses usable observation count and largest-remainder/original-name tie break; sampled axis is one half of a valid source length; strike is a source azimuth in radians; dip is a source dip in radians; every centre lies inside supplied bounds; invalid count/bounds fail clearly. Test a nontrivial automatic/manual set configuration and excluded rows through the extraction helper. Run nix develop -c pytest tests/interop/test_porepy.py -q. Run nix develop -c prek run --all-files. Before closing: br close with test evidence, br sync --flush-only, git add -f .beads/issues.jsonl plus source/test files, and commit --no-gpg-sign with this bead id.

title: Correct PorePy 3D axis semantics and validate generated CSV
description: Correct existing 3D PorePy export semantics and add 3D CSV validation in fractopo/interop/porepy.py, with tests in tests/interop/test_porepy.py. PorePy network_from_csv defines an elliptic row as CENTER_X,CENTER_Y,CENTER_Z,MAJOR_AXIS,MINOR_AXIS,MAJOR_AXIS_ANGLE,STRIKE_ANGLE,DIP_ANGLE; PorePy EllipticFracture stores major/minor values as radius-like semi-axes (r1/r2). fractopo input lengths are full observed trace/diameter lengths: EllipticalFracture.from_linestring_and_orientation and .from_structural_measurement must write major_axis == minor_axis == length / 2. Preserve centre and angle behavior. Add a check_porepy_3d_csv_format equivalent to existing 2D validation: ignore blank/comment lines, allow an optional first six-float domain row, require all subsequent rows to contain eight finite floats, require axes > 0, and for circular rows require equal axes. Public exports must call it before returning. Do not import/install PorePy; the project intentionally has no PorePy runtime dependency. Do not alter 2D behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove both existing 3D exporters emit exactly eight fields per fracture and output half the supplied trace/measurement length in both axis fields. Tests cover valid fractures-only CSV, valid domain-plus-fractures CSV, comments/blanks, and rejection of malformed/non-finite/non-positive-axis rows. Existing test expectations/docstrings reflect semi-axis values. Run nix develop -c pytest tests/interop/test_porepy.py -q. Run nix develop -c prek run --all-files. Before closing: br close with test evidence, br sync --flush-only, git add -f .beads/issues.jsonl plus source/test files, and commit --no-gpg-sign with this bead id.
